copy.heading: Go back to one moment
copy.body: You already made an attempt during setup. Now take one moment out of it and try that part again.
copy.transfer: Watch for a smaller moment this week where the same move would fit. You don’t have to use it today.

retry.direction: Try the same moment again in your own words.

copy.heading: Give the conversation one job
copy.body: Decide what this conversation is for, then whether now is a good time to have it.
practice_points: Name the job of the conversation.
Decide whether to continue, narrow the topic, return later, or move it to writing.

lessons.text: A conversation gets harder when you’re asking it to do five things at once. Choose the one job it needs to do today.
The job might be to understand, decide, ask for something, repair what happened, set a limit, or share something hard.
Then look at the conditions. You can shrink the topic, move it to another time, or put it in writing.
You don’t have to finish a conversation just because you started it.

quiz.prompt: Which version gives the conversation one clear job?

option_a.text: I need you to understand why I’m upset, apologize, agree I’m right, and decide bedtime tonight.

option_b.text: I want us to decide who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.

quiz.feedback_a: A is carrying four jobs. B asks for one decision: who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.
quiz.feedback_b: B asks for a single decision: who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.title: Bedtime needs an owner
scenario.scenario: You want to decide who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.
scenario.user_job: Open by saying what you want decided.
scenario.attempt_prompt: Open by saying what you want decided.
scenario.response_prompt: You have ten minutes. Narrow the topic, set a time to finish, or move the conversation to text.

copy.transfer: Next time something big is coming, ask yourself what you want the conversation to settle.

adam_line.text: I can talk, but I have to leave in ten minutes.

success_criteria: The timing, scope, or channel choice is usable

retry.direction: Use the same ten-minute limit. Change only the part Hope named.

modules.title: Spot what pressure makes you do

copy.heading: Spot what pressure makes you do
copy.body: Notice the first move you make after someone pushes back.

lessons.text: Pressure can change what you do next. That move is behavior, not a personality type.
You might talk faster, pile on proof, attack, go quiet, apologize your way out, or rush to fix it.
Listen for a move in your own recording. After my note, choose whether it fits what happened.

quiz.prompt: Which one names a move instead of a type?

option_b.text: When I hear “you’re overreacting,” I start listing older examples.

quiz.feedback_a: A labels the person. B names the cue and the move that followed.
quiz.feedback_b: B names the cue and the move that followed it.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: You’re explaining why the bedtime split has to change.
scenario.user_job: Say what’s wrong with the current split. A sentence or two.
scenario.attempt_prompt: Say what’s wrong with the current split. A sentence or two.
scenario.response_prompt: Answer him the way you’d actually answer.

copy.transfer: Listen for the first thing you do after pushback. You may start talking faster or reach back for older examples.

adam_line.text: Why is this suddenly such a big deal?

success_criteria: The note identifies one exact observable move
The learner can confirm or reject whether it fits

retry.direction: Answer the same objection. Change only the move I named.

copy.heading: Give yourself room to answer
copy.body: Take a moment after pushback, then pick one thing to say.

lessons.text: You don’t have to feel calm. Take enough time to choose what you say next.
After an objection, pick one move. Say a sentence, ask a question, or ask to come back to it.
Adding more words before you choose usually hides the move you meant to make.

quiz.prompt: Which one leaves room to choose?

option_a.text: No, listen, because last week you also, and the week before that…

option_b.text: (brief pause) The main thing I’m asking is whether you can own Tuesday bedtime.

quiz.feedback_a: A keeps adding evidence. B waits, then says one thing.
quiz.feedback_b: B waits, then makes one move the other person can answer.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: You have asked for a clearer bedtime schedule.
scenario.user_job: Listen to Adam. Take a moment. Then pick one thing to say.
scenario.response_prompt: Take a moment. Then say one sentence, ask one question, or ask to come back to it.

copy.transfer: When you catch yourself piling on words, stop there and pick one thing to say.

adam_line.text: I don’t see why we need a schedule. We’ve been figuring it out.

success_criteria: The response does not pile on evidence
The move is answerable or usable

retry.direction: Take a moment after the objection. Then make one move.

modules.title: Separate what happened from the story

copy.heading: Separate what happened from the story
copy.body: Say what happened so another person could point to the same event.

lessons.text: Start with something another person could point to: what was said, done, or agreed.
Stop before you turn what you think it means into a fact about them.
Your feelings can stay in. Leave out the verdict about what the event says about them.

quiz.prompt: Which one starts with something that happened?

option_a.text: You don’t care how exhausted I am.

option_b.text: I handled bedtime alone four nights this week after we agreed to split it.

quiz.feedback_a: A turns a motive into a fact. B gives a count and names the agreement.
quiz.feedback_b: B gives the other person something specific to answer.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: You want to tell Adam what this week has actually looked like.
scenario.user_job: Answer Adam with one current event, then stop.
scenario.response_prompt: Tell him what happened this week in a sentence or two. Stop before you say what it means about him.

copy.transfer: Prepare one current example for the real conversation. Don’t build a historical case file.

success_criteria: No motive or character claim is presented as fact
prohibited_inferences: that a feeling was expressed incorrectly

retry.direction: Give one thing that happened this week. Stop before you say what it proves.

modules.title: Keep one point in the room

copy.heading: Keep one point in the room
copy.body: Stay with your point after an objection you need to address.

lessons.text: Pick the point you want to keep clear, even when the conversation gets uncomfortable.
One example is enough. Stack up three and the other person answers the stack instead of the point.
When the other person objects, say you heard it. Then go back to the same point.

quiz.prompt: Which one is easier to stay on?

option_a.text: This is about bedtime, the dishes, your phone, your mother visiting, and how we never spend time together.

option_b.text: The point I need to keep clear is that bedtime needs an owner, not another list I manage.

quiz.feedback_a: A opens five issues at once. B leaves one thing to answer.
quiz.feedback_b: B keeps one point in view without building a case.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: You want bedtime to have a clear owner instead of another list you manage.
scenario.user_job: Say the point once. Then hold it after Adam’s objection.
scenario.attempt_prompt: Say the point once. Then hold it after Adam’s objection.
scenario.response_prompt: Respond to the part about work, then come back to bedtime. Leave the other issues for later.

copy.transfer: Say your one point out loud before the real conversation.

adam_line.text: I do bedtime when I can. Work has been all over the place.

success_criteria: At most one supporting example is used
The same point remains after resistance
prohibited_inferences: a universal word limit for a good answer

retry.direction: Answer the work concern briefly, then return to the bedtime request.

copy.heading: Make one answerable request
copy.body: Ask for one next step the other person can answer.

lessons.text: Turn the concern into a next step the other person can accept, decline, or change.
Say what, who, and when. Skip the parts that don’t matter.
A request leaves room for an answer. It isn’t a loyalty test, and a yes isn’t guaranteed.

quiz.prompt: Which one can the other person answer?

option_a.text: I need you to care more and show up for this family.

option_b.text: Can you own bedtime every Tuesday and Thursday, including pajamas, teeth, and lights out?

quiz.feedback_a: A asks for a quality. B asks for a job, a person, and two nights.
quiz.feedback_b: B gives the other person a clear request they can accept, decline, or change.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: You want to ask Adam to own bedtime on two specific nights.
scenario.user_job: Ask who will do what and on which nights.
scenario.attempt_prompt: Ask who will do what and on which nights.
scenario.response_prompt: Respond to the Thursday conflict. Adjust the nights or ask what would work.

copy.transfer: Try the request in a smaller conversation, or save it for the conversation you have in mind.

adam_line.text: Tuesday might work. Thursday I’m at work late.

success_criteria: One action or decision is identifiable
A time or condition is present when relevant
prohibited_inferences: that the request is a test of the partner’s love

retry.direction: Ask who will do what and when. Leave room for a no or a different plan.

modules.title: Put the week into one opener

copy.heading: Put the week into one opener
copy.body: Build one opener from the week, then respond to one pushback.

lessons.text: No new skill today. Put the week’s pieces into a single opener.
Say what you want settled, what happened this week, the point you want to keep clear, and what you’re asking for.
Then let Adam answer. If he pushes back, respond and return to the request.

quiz.prompt: Which opener is easier to answer?

option_a.text: You always leave everything to me, and I’m tired of being the only adult who notices anything.

option_b.text: Can we talk about bedtime? I handled it alone four nights this week. Can you take Tuesday and Thursday, from pajamas through lights out?

quiz.feedback_a: A opens with a verdict on the person. B opens with a count, a point, and a question that can be answered.
quiz.feedback_b: B gives a specific week and a request that can be answered.

scenario.heading: Tonight’s rep
scenario.scenario: Ask Adam to handle bedtime start to finish on two nights.
scenario.user_job: In your own words, say what you want settled, what happened, the point you want to keep clear, and your request.
scenario.attempt_prompt: In your own words, say what you want settled, what happened, the point you want to keep clear, and your request.
scenario.response_prompt: Respond to Adam’s pushback without opening a second argument. Then return to your request.

copy.transfer: Save one sentence from today’s practice for the real conversation.

approved_pushback_bank.text: I don’t think it’s that serious.
I’ve had a long day. Can this wait?
I thought we already handled this.

success_criteria: One point and request remain identifiable

retry.opener_direction: Run the opener again. Say what you want settled, what happened, and what you’re asking for.
retry.response_direction: Answer that pushback again. Address a relevant concern, or set aside a deflection, then return to the request.
